rules.title: Doubled braces escape a literal brace
rules.statement: In a format string, `{{` denotes a literal `{` and `}}` denotes a literal `}`; each doubled brace contributes exactly one brace to the literal output and is not treated as a placeholder delimiter.

rules.title: Unescaped `}` is an error
rules.statement: A `}` that is not part of a `}}` escape and does not close a placeholder is a compile error (`unmatched `}``); use `}}` to emit a literal `}`.

rules.title: Unterminated placeholder is an error
rules.statement: A `{` opening a placeholder must be closed by a matching `}`; if the placeholder body ends without `}`, it is a compile error (`unmatched `{``).

rules.title: Placeholder grammar
rules.statement: A placeholder has form `{` arg_id? (`:` format_spec)? `}` where arg_id is either an unsigned integer (explicit positional index) or an identifier (named argument); absence of arg_id means the next implicit positional argument.

rules.title: Implicit positional argument assignment
rules.statement: Placeholders without an explicit arg_id are assigned consecutive positional indices starting at 0, incremented per implicit placeholder; explicit-index and named placeholders do not advance this counter.

rules.title: Explicit-index vs named argument id
rules.statement: If the first arg_id char is a digit it is parsed as an explicit positional index; if it is an alphabetic char or `_` it is parsed as a named-argument identifier ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*).

rules.title: Format spec field ordering
rules.statement: After `:` the format spec fields appear in fixed order: (fill align)? sign? `#`? `0`? width? (`.` precision)? type? where align in {`<`,`>`,`^`}, sign in {`+`,`-`}, width and precision are unsigned integers, and type is a single char.

rules.title: Fill+align detection
rules.statement: A fill character is recognized only when immediately followed by an alignment marker (`<`,`>`,`^`), forming a 2-char fill+align prefix; a bare alignment marker uses the default fill; `<`=Left, `>`=Right, `^`=Center.

rules.title: Precision dot requires a number
rules.statement: A `.` in the format spec must be followed by an unsigned-integer precision; a `.` not followed by a digit is a compile error.
rules.divergence: Rust additionally permits `.*` and `.N$` precision forms; Logos here requires a literal number after `.`.

rules.title: Format type chars select a formatting trait
rules.statement: The type char selects the formatting trait: `?`=Debug, `x`=LowerHex, `X`=UpperHex, `o`=Octal, `b`=Binary, `e`=LowerExp, `E`=UpperExp; absence means Display; any other char before `}` is a compile error (`unknown type char`).

rules.title: Formatting-trait method names
rules.statement: Each formatting trait maps to a method name used by macro lowering: Display=`fmt`, Debug=`dbg`, LowerHex=`fmt_lower_hex`, UpperHex=`fmt_upper_hex`, Octal=`fmt_octal`, Binary=`fmt_binary`, LowerExp=`fmt_lower_exp`, UpperExp=`fmt_upper_exp`.

rules.title: Formatting-trait free-fn dispatchers
rules.statement: Format macro lowering dispatches via free-fn wrappers bound at sema-time through a generic trait bound (rather than a `.method()` dot-call): Display=`fmt_display`, Debug=`fmt_debug`, and hex/oct/bin/exp variants named identically to their method names.
